record.original_question: What relationship, if any, does the maximum likelihood degree of an algebraic statistical model have to the convergence properties of numerical statistical algorithms such as iterative proportional scaling and the EM algorithm?

evidence.quote: It is hoped that the ML degree is related to convergence properties of numerical algorithms used by statisticians, such as iterative proportional scaling or the EM algorithm, but no systematic study in this direction has yet been undertaken.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let M be an algebraic statistical model, i.e. a statistical model whose parameter space (or whose set of probability distributions) is described as the intersection of an algebraic variety with the probability simplex. Given i.i.d. data, the maximum likelihood estimation problem on M consists of maximizing the log-likelihood function over M. The maximum likelihood degree (ML degree) of M is defined as the number of complex critical points of the likelihood function on the Zariski closure of M, for generic data.

Two standard numerical procedures used to compute maximum likelihood estimates on such models are:
(i) iterative proportional scaling (IPS), used for hierarchical log-linear models on contingency tables, which cyclically rescales the current estimate to match observed marginal totals; and
(ii) the expectation–maximization (EM) algorithm, an iterative method that alternates between computing expected sufficient statistics under current parameter values and re-maximizing the complete-data log-likelihood.

Establish a precise relationship between the ML degree of M and the convergence behavior (e.g., rate of convergence, number of limit points, dependence on starting values, occurrence of local maxima, or computational complexity) of IPS and the EM algorithm when applied to M. In particular, determine whether and how the ML degree quantitatively governs or bounds the convergence properties of these algorithms.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up extensive literature on convergence of EM and on iterative proportional scaling (including modern optimization perspectives), and on the ML degree as an algebraic invariant, but no systematic results directly linking the ML degree of an algebraic statistical model to convergence rates or behavior of EM or IPS. The question appears to remain open, with no published comprehensive study addressing this specific relationship.

status_evidence.title: Iterative proportional scaling revisited: a modern optimization perspective
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes IPS convergence using coordinate descent and majorization-minimization, with no reference to ML degree.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence analyses of IPS are framed in optimization-theoretic terms, not in terms of the algebraic ML degree.

status_evidence.title: On some algorithms for estimation in Gaussian graphical models
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses algorithms for MLE in Gaussian graphical models including their convergence, without tying convergence to ML degree.
status_evidence.claim: Recent algorithmic work on MLE in algebraic models does not relate convergence properties to ML degree.
